title: System Hacking

objectives.text: Name the four system hacking phases in order and map each to the ATT&CK tactic a defender monitors
Tell horizontal from vertical privilege escalation and name the hardening that blocks each common category
Recognise persistence and rootkit indicators (new services, scheduled tasks, Run keys, hidden files) and the controls that detect them
Explain steganography as a way to hide data, and name the signs and tools used to detect it (steganalysis)
Recognise log clearing from its events and explain why central log forwarding and write-once storage defeat it

readingMap.why: The lifecycle and password-attack families are tested often; the app has notes only for this section, so study its details on your own (see Self-study).
Escalation categories and their hardening are frequent scenario questions.
Rootkit types, persistence locations and steganography appear as recall and tool questions.
Log-clearing events and the controls against them are short, reliable points.

feynmanPrompts: Explain the four system hacking phases to a colleague, and for each one say what a defender would see in the logs.
Explain the difference between a user-mode and a kernel-mode rootkit, and why secure boot and integrity monitoring help against the second.
Explain why forwarding logs to a central server as they are written makes clearing the local logs much less useful to an attacker.
